title: The Tall Country
subtitle: North of the singing wood the land climbs into high pasture, and the walls there were built for people three times our height.
tagline: Ogres in the valley, owlbears in the orchard, and a goblin with a cart-chain. Five chapters.

map.alt: A hand-drawn map of the Tall Country: Harrowdale in the valley, Tobin's farm, the giants' orchard, the bridge over the gorge, the nest ledges and the high hall on the ridge

ending_note: The fires are out in the high hall. Every chapter stays open: play any of them again.

shots.title: The Tall Country
shots.text: Above Harrowdale the road climbs into the Tall Country, where the giants built their houses and their walls, and then went away.
For a hundred years nothing came down from up there but weather. This autumn the ogres came down. Twice in a month.
The reeve of Harrowdale paid us to find out why, and to make it stop. I am Mara, and I kept this account, because nobody else would.

shots.title: Chapter 1 · The Broken Fence
shots.text: We waited at Tobin's farm, which the ogre had visited twice already. It came a third time, at dusk, as if keeping an appointment.
It was not alone. Goblins ran ahead of it with torches, the way dogs run ahead of a hunter.
Ilyra said the pens were our friend. A thing that size cannot follow you through a gap meant for sheep.
The ogre wore an iron collar, and the skin under it was burned. Ogres do not put collars on each other.
The goblins' torches smelled of pitch from the high hall's stores. Someone up there was driving the big ones down.

shots.title: Chapter 2 · Feathers in the Briar
shots.text: The quickest way up the ridge goes through the giants' orchard. The trees still fruit, and the fruit is the size of a barrel.
Something nests there now. Chruna found feathers as long as her arm, and fur caught in the briars beside them.
Vesper said owlbears hate noise. Then he started playing anyway, because the wasps were already coming.
The owlbear had a chain on its leg too, snapped short. It had pulled free of something and come here to hide.
Beyond the orchard the giant-road begins. Chruna said whoever chains owlbears will be waiting on it.

shots.title: Chapter 3 · The Toll of the Giant-Road
shots.text: Halfway up, the giant-road crosses a gorge on a bridge built for giants. Someone has put a gate on it and a sign that says TOLL.
Bugbears keep the gate. An ogre keeps the bugbears. The toll, they told us, was everything we carried and one of us.
Curogana asked whether the ogre could be paid in lightning. Guy said we would find out.
The bugbears kept a ledger. Sheep, carts, travellers, and in a column of its own: ogres, delivered to Skarrow.
Skarrow. Every name led back to him, and to the smoke on the ridge.

shots.title: Chapter 4 · The Mother of the Nest
shots.text: Below the hall the cliff is all ledges, and on the widest ledge two owlbears had made a nest. They were not chained. They were guarding something.
Harpies sat on the rocks above them and sang. Whatever they sing, you want to walk toward it, and the ledge is narrow.
Ilyra tied us together on the narrow part. Guy said it was the most romantic thing anyone had done for him in years.
In the nest were cubs, and a goblin snare. Skarrow had been taking the young to make the parents fight for him.
Elion cut the snare and left the cubs where they were. Above us the doors of the high hall stood open. They were twenty feet tall.

shots.title: Chapter 5 · Skarrow's Hall
shots.text: The high hall was built for giants, and Skarrow had filled it with chains. Two ogres stood in it, collared, with braziers behind them.
Skarrow was the smallest thing in the room, and he sat on a throne he could have slept in. He held a cart-chain and a torch, and the ogres watched the torch.
He told us the valley would be his by midwinter. I told him the valley had hired us.
When Skarrow fell, the ogres stood still for a long time. Then Chruna broke their collars, and they walked out into the snow and up into the hills, and did not look back.
We put out the fires. The hall was quiet in a way it had not been for a hundred years.
No ogre came down to Harrowdale that winter. Tobin mended his gate, and made it wider, just in case.
In spring Elion went back to the orchard and found tracks in the mud, small ones beside big ones.
The Tall Country goes on further north than anyone has walked. That, the reeve said, is a job for next year.
